difficultyRationale: Requires distinguishing a cohesion problem from superficially similar coupling or naming concerns.
explanation: Cohesion measures how closely a class's members work together toward one purpose. Tax calculation, email delivery, analytics, shipping-label generation, and PDF rendering each belong to a different concern with its own reason to change, so grouping all of them inside OrderProcessor is a textbook low-cohesion design. Extracting each responsibility into its own class, collaborating with OrderProcessor, is the standard fix.

options.text: The class is fine as long as every method is public and well-named, since cohesion is only about naming clarity.
options.explanation: Cohesion is about whether a class's responsibilities belong together conceptually, not about naming; even perfectly named methods for six unrelated concerns still make the class low-cohesion.

options.text: The class has a coupling problem, not a cohesion problem, because it depends on an email sender and a PDF library, and that external coupling is what should be reduced through dependency injection rather than by regrouping its responsibilities.
options.explanation: Depending on external collaborators is a coupling concern, but the issue described here is that unrelated responsibilities are bundled inside the class's own methods -- that is a cohesion problem about the class's internal design, separate from how many external dependencies it has.

options.text: The class has low cohesion because it bundles unrelated responsibilities that each change for a different reason; each responsibility should be extracted into its own class that OrderProcessor collaborates with.
options.explanation: Cohesion measures how closely a class's members work together toward one purpose. Tax calculation, email sending, analytics, and PDF rendering each belong to a different concern with its own reason to change, so grouping them in one class is a textbook low-cohesion design; splitting the class by responsibility is the standard remedy.

options.text: The class should be fixed by making every method static so each can be called independently without an object.
options.explanation: Making methods static doesn't address why unrelated responsibilities are grouped together; it would keep the same mixed responsibilities in the same class, just accessed differently.
